title: The Promise of the Old Mill House
premise: Astrid Galloway has spent eleven years orchestrating other people's perfect days while quietly dismantling his own capacity for one, ever since the summer he left Millbrook without saying goodbye to Wren Halloway, the woman he loved and lied to. When a letter he wrote and never mailed surfaces during the restoration of the old mill house—postmarked, impossibly, eleven years ago—he returns to find Wren engaged to a man who offers her everything Astrid couldn't: honesty, permanence, a future without secrets. As Astrid plans her wedding, the two are forced to confront what really happened the night he left, including the truth about his family's ruin and the promise they made beneath the mill's broken wheel. In the end, Astrid must choose between protecting Wren's happiness and claiming his own, and when she calls off the wedding not for him but for herself, they meet at the mill house on the anniversary of their promise—older, scarred, and finally ready to risk the whole heart.
about_author: Felix Coldharbour is the pen name of a former estate auctioneer who spent a decade cataloguing the letters, photographs, and unfinished promises left behind in old houses. He writes romances about people who mistake silence for kindness, from a converted granary on the northern coast.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Other People's Happiness
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A flawless society wedding in Boston collapses into rain and recriminations, and Astrid realizes he no longer believes in the vows he sells. That night, a solicitor's email arrives: the old mill house in Millbrook is being restored, and workers found something with his name on it. Emotional beat: hollow success cracking open.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He drives back to Millbrook and receives an unopened letter in his own handwriting, postmarked the week he fled town—a letter he has no memory of mailing. Reading it, he confronts the boy who promised Wren everything. Emotional beat: vertigo of a past that refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Mill House
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, now the restoration project's architect, finds Astrid standing in the doorway of her site—and learns he'll be coordinating her engagement party there. Old fury and older tenderness collide over sawdust and blueprints. Emotional beat: the shock of seeing the ghost made flesh.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Astrid agrees to plan the wedding as penance; Wren allows it to prove she's moved on. Their professional truce is strained by small betrayals of memory—the song, the cider apples, the way she still says his name like a question. Emotional beat: proximity masquerading as indifference.

chapters.title: What Daniel Doesn't Ask
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Her fiancé Daniel is kind, steady, and incurious in ways Wren once mistook for peace. When he dismisses the mill house's history as 'sentimental clutter,' Wren begins cataloguing what a life with him would require her to forget. Emotional beat: loyalty examined and found load-bearing but cracked.

chapters.title: The Night the Wheel Broke
chapters.summary: Dual POV flashback. Eleven years earlier: the Galloway family's bankruptcy, Astrid's father's disgrace, and the lie Astrid told Wren—that he was leaving because he didn't love her—to spare her the fall. The chapter reveals the letter was written that night and slipped into the mill wall, never meant to be found. Emotional beat: the origin wound exposed.

chapters.title: Rumors in a Small Town
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A local gossip spots them laughing together at the mill; word reaches Daniel, then Wren's mother, who always blamed Astrid for Wren's lost decade. Astrid, offered a lucrative contract in Paris, must decide whether staying is courage or selfishness. Emotional beat: rising pressure from every side.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Behind the mill's wheel housing, workers uncover a second letter—Wren's own, written the night she waited for him and he never came. Reading her younger self's heartbreak beside his confession, she understands the shape of the lie that broke them both. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into clarity.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the engagement party Astrid planned, the truth detonates: Daniel, having read the found letters, asks Wren plainly whether she's marrying him or hiding from Astrid. Wren, refusing to be anyone's consolation prize—including Astrid's—cancels the wedding herself and walks out into the storm. Emotional beat: everything honest and nothing safe.

chapters.title: Under the Turning Wheel
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, brief coda in Wren's. One year later, the restored mill house opens—not as a venue, but as Wren's studio, with Astrid's office in the old grain loft. On the anniversary of their promise, they exchange new vows with no guests, no planner, no lies. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.
